prompt: What is a good durable workflow engine for AI tasks with retries?

result.text:
When building AI tasks, pipelines, or multi-step agent loops that require robust retries, state persistence, and error handling, several durable workflow engines stand out depending on your stack and deployment preferences:

1. Temporal (The Industry Standard for Code-As-Workflow)

Best for: Complex, long-running agentic loops, enterprise-grade reliability, and polyglot architectures.

Why it fits AI tasks: Temporal treats your workflow as code (available in Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, etc.). It automatically checkpoints every step. If an LLM API rate-limits, times out, or your server crashes mid-execution, Temporal isolates the failure to that specific "activity," retries it with exponential backoff, and resumes the workflow right where it left off without re-running previous expensive model calls.

Trade-off: Requires running a Temporal Cluster (though Temporal Cloud abstracts this).

2. Inngest (Best for TypeScript & Serverless/Web Applications)

Best for: Developers building AI features inside web apps, serverless environments, or standard Node.js/TypeScript codebases.

Why it fits AI tasks: Inngest lets you write background jobs and step-based workflows using native code without provisioning complex state-machine infrastructure. It provides built-in rate-limiting, concurrency controls, automatic step-level retries, and step checkpointing. It integrates smoothly with modern AI frameworks (like the Vercel AI SDK).

Trade-off: Primarily optimized for TypeScript/JavaScript ecosystems.

3. Prefect or Dagster (Best for Data Pipelines & Heavy LLM Processing)

Best for: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines, batch document processing, embedding generation, and data-heavy AI workflows.

Why it fits AI tasks: While historically built for data engineering, their modern task-orchestration models handle retries, timeouts, and state tracking natively. If your AI task involves heavy data preparation, chunking, and calling LLMs across thousands of files, these tools offer unmatched visibility and data lineage.

Trade-off: Less suited for real-time, event-driven agent loops compared to Temporal or Inngest.

Key Architectural Rule for AI Workflows

Whichever engine you choose, remember the golden rule of durable AI workflows: Isolate non-deterministic code (like LLM generations or random tool outputs) into isolated "activities" or "steps." Because workflow engines use replay mechanics to recover from crashes, your core workflow logic must remain deterministic, letting the engine record and replay the saved outputs of your AI calls.
